- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.2) or when recent prices show strong downward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model tends to overreact and peak too high, then corrects sharply.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often fails to adjust downward quickly after prolonged high prices, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early summer (June) when sentiment is volatile and prices show strong downward correction.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days before forecast horizon, model should adjust downward to reflect sentiment lag.
- Avoid extrapolating upward trends when sentiment is weak or mixed — model tends to ignore sentiment when it’s low or erratic.
